/-!
# Erdős Problem 951

*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/951](https://www.erdosproblems.com/951)
 - [Er77c] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III. Number theory day (Proc. Conf., Rockefeller Univ.,
    New York, 1976) (1977), 43-72.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped Finsupp Nat.Prime Topology
open Filter

namespace Erdos951

/-- A sequence `a : ℕ → ℝ` is said to have property `Erdos951Prop` if for any pair of distinct
finitely supported sequences `k l : ℕ →₀ ℕ` their corresponding Beurling integers are of distance
at least one apart. -/
def Erdos951Prop (a : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (k ℓ : ℕ →₀ ℕ), k ≠ ℓ → |beurlingInteger a k - beurlingInteger a ℓ| ≥ 1

/-- If a strictly increasing sequence `a : ℕ → ℝ` has property `Erdos951Prop`
and `1 < a 0`, then `a` is a sequence of Beurling prime numbers. -/
@[category API, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_951.variants.isBeurlingPrimes {a : ℕ → ℝ} (ha : 1 < a 0)
    (hm : StrictMono a) (he : Erdos951Prop a) :
    IsBeurlingPrimes a := by
  refine ⟨ha, hm, tendsto_atTop_atTop.2 fun x => ?_⟩
  by_contra h_contra
  obtain ⟨L, hL⟩ : ∃ L, Filter.Tendsto a Filter.atTop (𝓝 L) :=
    ⟨_, tendsto_atTop_isLUB hm.monotone (isLUB_ciSup ⟨x, Set.forall_mem_range.2 fun n =>
    le_of_not_ge fun hn => h_contra ⟨n, fun m hm' => hn.trans (hm.monotone hm')⟩⟩)⟩
  obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ := Metric.tendsto_atTop.mp hL (1 / 2) (by norm_num)
  have := hm (by linarith : N < N + 1)
  have h_diff : a (N + 1) - a N ≥ 1 := by
    rw [← abs_of_nonneg (by linarith : 0 ≤ a _ - _)]
    simpa using he (.single (N + 1) 1) (.single N 1) (by simpa [Finsupp.ext_iff] using ⟨N, by simp⟩)
  linarith [abs_lt.1 (hN N le_rfl), abs_lt.1 (hN (N + 1) (by grind))]

/-- If `1 < a 0 < ...` has property `Erdos951Prop`, is it true that `#{a i ≤ x} ≤ π x`? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_951 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ a : ℕ → ℝ, 1 < a 0 → StrictMono a → Erdos951Prop a →
      ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, {i : ℕ | a i ≤ x}.ncard ≤ π ⌊x⌋₊ := by
  sorry

/-- Beurling conjectured that if `1 < a 0 < a 1 < ⋯` has property `Erdos951Prop` and the number
of reals in $[1, x]$ of the form $\prod_i a_i^{k_i}$ is $x + o(\log x)$, then `a` must be the
sequence of primes. Property `Erdos951Prop` makes distinct exponent vectors give distinct
Beurling integers, so counting the set `BeurlingIntegers a` counts the generalised integers. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_951.variants.beurling :
    ∀ a : ℕ → ℝ, IsBeurlingPrimes a → Erdos951Prop a →
    ((fun x => (BeurlingIntegers a ∩ .Iic x).ncard - x) =o[atTop] Real.log) →
    a = Nat.cast ∘ Nat.nth Nat.Prime := by
  sorry

end Erdos951

findings.description:
The docstring presents this as Beurling's conjecture, but the Lean adds the hypothesis `Erdos951Prop a`: all generalised integers are pairwise at least 1 apart. In the source, that separation is H. N. Shapiro's hypothesis for the main question (13). It is not a hypothesis of Beurling's conjecture (12), which concerns an arbitrary sequence 1 < P_1 < P_2 < ⋯. The docstring's claim that Beurling assumed `Erdos951Prop` is therefore wrong.

The extra hypothesis changes the claim substantially: under `Erdos951Prop`, density 1 alone forces a = primes. So the Lean statement is a much weaker claim, true by an elementary argument, in which Beurling's o(log x) threshold plays no role. Sketch (my own argument, not from a source), with S = `BeurlingIntegers a` and B(x) = #(S ∩ [1,x]):

(1) All elements of S are integers. Since S is 1-separated, each cell [n,n+1) holds at most one element, and B(x) = x + o(x) leaves only o(x) empty cells up to x. If cells n and n+1 hold n+f_n and n+1+f_{n+1}, separation forces f_{n+1} ≥ f_n, so the fractional offset f is nondecreasing along runs of occupied cells. Suppose s = m+θ ∈ S with θ ∈ (0,1). Then s·t_{n+1} − s·t_n = m + θ + s(f_{n+1} − f_n). Whenever the target cells in between are occupied and s(f_{n+1} − f_n) < 1 − θ, the offset of s·t_{n+1} must exceed that of s·t_n by at least θ; otherwise it wraps around and decreases. This can happen fewer than 1/θ times in a row. The interruptions (source gaps, target gaps, and fewer than s/(1−θ) large offset jumps per run) number o(x), contradicting the x − o(x) consecutive steps.

(2) S = ℕ. Let p be the least positive integer not in S; p is prime. The integers n with v_p(n) = 1 have positive density, and each one in S equals g·h with g a generator satisfying v_p(g) = 1 and p ∤ h. Two such generators g₁ = pd₁ ≠ g₂ = pd₂ would give g₁·(d₂k) = g₂·(d₁k), with d₁k, d₂k ∈ S for suitable k. That is two distinct exponent vectors with the same value, contradicting `Erdos951Prop`. A single such generator g = pd with d ≥ 2 covers density at most (1−1/p)/(2p) < (1/p)(1−1/p). Hence S = ℕ and the generators are the primes.

Beurling's conjecture implies the Lean statement, but not conversely: the Lean statement is provable while the conjecture for non-separated systems stays open, so the two can differ in truth value.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős [Er80], 'A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory', Ann. Discrete Math. 6 (1980), p. 103 (Rényi archive 1980-03.pdf): "The following nice conjecture is due to Beurling. Let 1 < P_1 < ⋯ be a sequence of real numbers. b_1 < b_2 < ⋯ is the set of real numbers of the form ∏ P_i^{α_i} where the α_i are non-negative integers. Assume that B(x) = ∑_{b_i ≤ x} 1 = x + o(log x). (12) Then the P's are the primes. It is not hard to see that if (12) is true it is best possible. In this connection H.N. Shapiro asked the following question: Assume that the numbers ∏ P_i^{α_i} differ by at least one. Is it then true that ∑_{P_i ≤ x} 1 ≤ π(x), (13) the equality occurring only if the P's are the primes?" erdosproblems.com/951 (LaTeX source): "Beurling conjectured that if the number of reals in [1,x] of the form ∏ a_i^{k_i} is x+o(log x) then the a_i must be the sequence of primes." Neither text puts the separation condition in Beurling's conjecture.
findings.suggested_fix:
State Beurling's conjecture for general Beurling prime systems, counting generalised integers with multiplicity (that is, counting exponent vectors), and drop `Erdos951Prop`:

@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_951.variants.beurling :
    ∀ a : ℕ → ℝ, IsBeurlingPrimes a →
    ((fun x => ({k : ℕ →₀ ℕ | beurlingInteger a k ≤ x}.ncard : ℝ) - x) =o[atTop] Real.log) →
    a = Nat.cast ∘ Nat.nth Nat.Prime

I checked that this typechecks. The set is finite because a → ∞ and a 0 > 1. Do not just delete `Erdos951Prop` and keep the set count `(BeurlingIntegers a ∩ .Iic x).ncard`: that version is false. For a = 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 11, … (the primes with 4 inserted), `BeurlingIntegers a` = ℕ≥1 and the count is ⌊x⌋ = x + O(1). Update the docstring accordingly. The alternative is to keep the current text but document it as Beurling's conjecture restricted to `Erdos951Prop` sequences; that version is provable, even under B(x) = x + o(x).

findings.description: The docstring asks "is it true that `#{a i ≤ x} ≤ π x`?" and gives no quantifier over x. The Lean states the inequality only for all sufficiently large x (`∀ᶠ x in atTop`). The source says the 'for all x' reading is disproved, so the docstring should say which reading is formalized; otherwise a reader may think the statement is the disproved version and the `research open` tag is stale. The mathematics is unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: erdosproblems.com/951: "It is unclear whether this is intended to hold for all x or just all sufficiently large x. The former question can be disproved by finite calculation ... A finite counterexample for x=10 was found by ChatGPT-5.2 Pro (prompted by Leeham)." Status: OPEN.
findings.suggested_fix: Docstring: "If $1 < a_0 < a_1 < \cdots$ has property `Erdos951Prop`, is it true that $\#\{i : a_i \le x\} \le \pi(x)$ for all sufficiently large $x$? (The version for all $x$ is false.)"

review.notes:
`erdos_951` formalizes the 'for all sufficiently large x' reading with real x, a threshold that depends on a, and π(x) = `Nat.primeCounting ⌊x⌋₊`. This is exactly the reading erdosproblems.com lists as OPEN. The 'for all x' reading is disproved: a counterexample at x = 10 (ChatGPT-5.2 Pro, prompted by Leeham) and further ones at x = 5−ε, 7−ε, … by Sothanaphan. Thomas Bloom states on the forum that the asymptotic question was intended. So the statement and its `research open` tag match the source.

The `answer(sorry)` slot has the right polarity: a positive answer means the inequality holds. The set {i | a i ≤ x} is always finite here, because `isBeurlingPrimes` shows a → ∞, so the value 0 that `ncard` gives an infinite set is never reached.

Erdős's extra sub-question in [Er80] (does equality hold only for the primes?) is not formalized. That is an omission, not a defect.

`Erdos951Prop` matches the source's hypothesis. `erdos_951.variants.isBeurlingPrimes` is proved and depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

In the Beurling variant, the `Tendsto a atTop atTop` part of `IsBeurlingPrimes` is harmless: for a bounded sequence the product set is eventually infinite, so its `ncard` is 0 and the o(log x) hypothesis fails anyway.

Erdős's own wording of Beurling's conjecture counts the set of distinct products (b_1 < b_2 < ⋯). Read literally for general sequences it is trivially false (primes with 4 inserted), so the intended count must be with multiplicity, as is standard for Beurling systems. That is why the suggested fix counts exponent vectors rather than just deleting `Erdos951Prop`.

not_demonstrated.reason: As stated in the file the theorem is true and its hypotheses are satisfiable (the primes satisfy them), so there is neither a vacuity proof nor a counterexample. Showing that the added `Erdos951Prop` makes the statement weaker than Beurling's conjecture but still provable needs a genuine counting and density argument: all Beurling integers are integers, then they are all of ℕ, then a = primes. Formalizing that is far beyond a few lines.

submission.summary: I made no trivial-proof file. The reported misformalization of `erdos_951.variants.beurling` (the extra `Erdos951Prop` hypothesis) produces a true, non-vacuous statement whose proof needs real mathematics. Nothing short and honest can be proved or refuted, so I bailed out as the rules allow.
submission.gave_up_reason: The only misformalization I reported is `Erdos951.erdos_951.variants.beurling`. It adds `Erdos951Prop` to Beurling's conjecture. As stated in the file, the theorem is neither vacuous nor false. The primes satisfy every hypothesis: `IsBeurlingPrimes`, `Erdos951Prop`, and the count minus x equals ⌊x⌋₊ − x, which is bounded and so o(log x). So an unsatisfiable hypothesis gives no shortcut, and there is no counterexample to exhibit. The defect is that the restricted statement is a much weaker claim that is actually true, whereas Beurling's conjecture is open. Proving it takes a page of real mathematics: an argument on fractional offsets showing that a 1-separated multiplicative semigroup of density 1 contains only integers, then a p-adic density argument showing it is all of ℕ, then deducing a = `Nat.nth Nat.Prime`. In Lean that would be hundreds of lines, not a few. A quick check such as ¬`Erdos951Prop` for the primes with 4 inserted would only restate that the hypothesis narrows the class of sequences, which is intended and not in dispute, so it would not show the defect. My other finding (a missing "for all sufficiently large x" in the docstring of `erdos_951`) is minor, not a misformalization. I did not create `/workspace/review/trivial_proof.lean`, so there is nothing to delete.

submission.summary: Rewrote `erdos_951.variants.beurling` to state Beurling's conjecture as in [Er80, p. 103] and erdosproblems.com/951. Dropped the extra hypothesis `Erdos951Prop a`, which is Shapiro's separation condition and not Beurling's. Generalised integers are now counted with multiplicity (exponent vectors): `({k : ℕ →₀ ℕ | beurlingInteger a k ≤ x}.ncard : ℝ) - x =o[atTop] Real.log`. Merely dropping the hypothesis while keeping the count of distinct values would have been false (primes with 4 inserted). Changed the category from `research solved` to `research open`, since the source gives it only as a conjecture and I found no resolution. Rewrote its docstring and added [Er80] to the module references. Also applied the trivial docstring fix for `erdos_951` ("for all sufficiently large `x`"); its statement is unchanged. The file compiles with only the two `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings. On a copy of the edited file in /workspace/review I checked the elaborated statement and proved that the corrected statement implies the old restricted one. Only 951.lean was edited; lakefile.toml and run/ were already modified before I started and are untouched.
